qualityNotes: High-quality healthcare with excellent hospitals in Brussels, Antwerp, and Ghent. Most doctors speak English in addition to French/Dutch/German.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open Mon-Fri 9am-6pm, Sat 9am-12pm. Duty pharmacies (pharmacie de garde) available nights/weekends — check apotheek.be or pharmacie.be
pharmacyTips: Look for the green cross sign. Pharmacists are well-trained and can advise on minor ailments. Many OTC products require asking the pharmacist (behind counter but no prescription needed).
prescriptionRules: Most antibiotics and stronger medications require a prescription from a Belgian or EU doctor. EU prescriptions are generally accepted.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine (high-dose)
restrictedMeds.note: Low-dose codeine available OTC, higher doses require prescription

restrictedMeds.name: Benzodiazepines
restrictedMeds.note: Prescription required, bring documentation if carrying personal supply

bringDocumentation: EU citizens can use the European Health Insurance Card (EHIC). Non-EU travelers should carry prescriptions in English, ideally with generic drug names. No special import certificate needed for personal-use quantities.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Required for Schengen visa applicants (minimum €30,000 medical coverage)
travelInsurance.tips: Belgium is part of the Schengen Area. If you need a Schengen visa, travel insurance is mandatory. EU/EEA citizens can use EHIC for reduced-cost care.

vaccinations.notes: No special vaccinations required for most travelers. Tick-borne encephalitis is not a significant risk.

waterNotes: Tap water is safe and high quality throughout Belgium.
foodSafetyTips: Excellent food safety standards. Street food (frites, waffles) is safe. Mussels and other seafood are fresh and well-regulated.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Belgium. Emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, EU health insurance (EHIC), medication restrictions, and travel insurance requirements.

hospitals.name: Cliniques Universitaires Saint-Luc
hospitals.notes: Major university hospital. French and English speaking.

dentalCare.availability: Good dental care. EHIC covers emergency dental for EU citizens.
dentalCare.notes: Belgian dental care is affordable by Western European standards.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: 1813 (Zelfmoordlijn — Dutch); 0800 32 123 (Centre de Prévention du Suicide — French)
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Available in Brussels, which is highly international.
mentalHealth.notes: Belgium has good mental health services. Brussels has many English-speaking therapists due to the EU/NATO presence.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Belgium has good accessibility in modern areas. Historic city centers (Bruges, Ghent) with cobblestones can be challenging.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Brussels Metro has elevator access. STIB/MIVB buses are low-floor. SNCB trains offer assistance for disabled travelers.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Bruges is walkable but cobblestones are difficult for wheelchairs. Ghent's tram system is accessible.

insuranceClaimProcess: Belgian healthcare uses a reimbursement system. Keep attestation de soins (care certificates) from doctors. EU citizens with EHIC get partial reimbursement. Non-EU visitors pay upfront and claim from travel insurance.
